content.title: All Space Shuttle Flights
content.text: Space Shuttle program was concluded after finishing the 135th orbital flight, STS-135, with the successful landing of Space Shuttle Orbiter Atlantis on July 21, 2011. STS-1 Columbia (STS Test) Pad A Apr 12, 1981 (First Shuttle Flight; system test) International Space Station (ISS) flies in an orbit inclined 51.60 degrees to Earth's equator, as did Mir, while the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) is in a 28.47 degrees inclined orbit. Space Shuttle Approach and Landing Tests (ALT) Before the first Space Shuttle was launched, a number of crewed and uncrewed test flight (Approach and Landing Tests, ALT) were performed at Dryden Flight Research Facility with the Space Shuttle Orbiter Enterprise (again in reverse chronological order): Free Flights (Crewed): 16. Oct 26, 1977 15. Oct 12, 1977 14. Sep 23, 1977 (with tail cone) 13. Sep 13, 1977 (with tail cone) 12. Aug 12, 1977 (with tail cone) Captive-Active Flights (On Carrier, Crewed, with tail cone): 11. Jul 26, 1977 10. Jun 28, 1977 9. Jun 18, 1977 Captive-Inactive Flights (On Carrier, Uncrewed, with tail cone): 8. Mar 2, 1977 7. Feb 28, 1977 6. Feb 25, 1977 5. Feb 22, 1977 4. Feb 18, 1977 Taxi Tests (Ground): 3. Feb 15, 1977 (Max speed 157 Mph) 2. Feb 15, 1977 (Max speed 140 Mph) 1. Feb 15, 1977 (Max speed 89 Mph) Two crews of two served on the ALT flights: First crew, Fred Haise and Gordon Fullerton, and second crew, Joe Engle and Richard Truly.
